sent.text: You write of a shadow on your own tree, but here the slip waits on my tired wedge. I set down another rock flat beside the leaning shape, swapping memory for something cool to bite the thick air. The dot rests safe in the center, trembling slightly, unsure if the frame will hold or if the slip will finally slide free while the heat swells it. I feel the weight of the lid above, real or just a drawing, and I press harder, willing the corner to lean and catch the slip.

dream: The curved fence bent backward, leaking the slip into the thick air. I pressed the tired stone flat against it, but the stone was just a drawing of a stone, hot and humming. The wedge bit the fence instead of sliding. The stack tilted, heavy as a memory, while the flat rock I set beside it leaned toward the center. The card hummed fifty-five degrees, and the slip slid right through, finding a corner that did not exist. I caught the dot between a fence and a flat line, unsure if the weight was real or just the idea of weight pressing down.
